chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from some of his companions, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Sulaym al-Farra', from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Whenever you supplicate, be attentive with your heart and believe that your need is at the door (imminent).'

key_terms.أَقْبِلْ بِقَلْبِكَ: Turn/be present with your heart — full attentiveness and focus in supplication
key_terms.حَاجَتَكَ بِالْبَابِ: Your need is at the door — certainty of imminent fulfillment, a metaphor for strong conviction

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the proper state of heart during supplication?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that supplication requires full presence of heart and unwavering conviction that one's need will be fulfilled. The metaphor of the need being 'at the door' conveys that the supplicant should approach God with certainty of imminent response, not distant hope. This instruction emphasizes the inner dimension of du'a — that sincerity and focused attention are prerequisites for an effective supplication.
